text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- United Nigeria Congress Party (UNCP) takes lead in local government elections, topping other parties put together; it and Democratic Party of Nigeria, also doing well, want military leader General Sani Abacha to be their presidential candidate in elections next year.
- Last civilian head of state Shehu Shagari backs Abacha for presidency
- Domestic air fares rise 100 percent from today Monday. Return ticket to Abuja from Lagos now 10,160 naira.

- Finance Minister Anthony Ani says government has given approval for loans disbursed to the World Bank-assisted Small and Medium-scale Enterprises project to be repaid at the official exchange rate of 22 naira to the dollar.
- Personal charisma and individual influence appear to have determined how people voted in local elections.
- Cost of credit soars in banks
- UNCP shoots ahead in local government polls
- State-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corp imports 38,000 tonnes of petroleum products to augment local supplies.
- Nigeria's population to hit 128.7 million in 2000, according to federal government and United Nations Population Fund projections.
